links.comparator_used: No comparison with periodic labeled audits; the study compared 2σ vs 3σ control limits and model A vs model B against baseline limits set from the first 150 cases
links.outcome: Detection of performance drift and model switching using statistical process control charts of auto-segmentation agreement (DSC, HD95, SDSC)
links.effect: Model A stayed mostly within 3σ limits (9-13 months per organ). Model B was flagged as a marked shift (p < 0.001), with all five organs outside both thresholds in all 7 months. 2σ limits were more sensitive to mild deviations in model A.
links.tradeoff: The 2σ criterion may be too general to detect all outliers and is limited with interobserver variability. The design was retrospective and single-site. Model A's original AI contours were not archived, so model B contours were used as the reference, which may confound the model comparison.
links.quote: The monitoring system using process behavior charts effectively detected out-of-distribution outliers for prostate, bladder, rectum, fem_head_l, and fem_head_r, providing a reliable and easy-to-use framework for quality assurance and early detection of clinical practice change.
